rationale: Review of direct check a7ab7f88 (unit-claim-heartbeat-header-gate), whose fresh execution 1987811182294bfbb372a36548be8d8b completed the comparison with prerequisites matched (scenario 0, normal-rejected 1), comparison_complete and witness_complete true at witness index 2, and outcome violated. This review supplies the required checker_correspondence item and resolves the two open applicability issues, which record the same threading conflict (processHeartbeat's comment versus the transport's concurrent usage) against the claim and against the revised harness legality.

review_items.rationale: Requirement versus encoded predicate: the obligation requires the RPC-header compatibility decision to reach every AppendEntries entry point; the property asserts that for the declared out-of-window heartbeat the fast path left term, state, leader identity and last contact unchanged (guard_applied true). Entry and caller duties: the harness declares out_of_window_protocol_version true and independently establishes, on the normal path, that the same request shape is rejected with ErrUnsupportedProtocol and changes nothing (declared prerequisite normal-rejected), which is what entitles the fast-path event to be compared against the guard rather than against an unexamined assumption about the request. Identity: op_id hb-1 is on the declaration, the normal-path prerequisite and the fast-path result, and the correlation matched all three. Oracle: the assertion is computed from emitted event fields, not from tests_passed; the run exited 0 while guard_applied is false, which is exactly the case the oracle must catch. Observation path and completion: processHeartbeat is the callback body installed by SetHeartbeatHandler (compared with the library's own handler in S44), both handlers responded on their channels, and the run completed with exit 0. Concurrency: the nodes are built with skipStartup so no main loop runs, which is disclosed as an adaptation; it removes the race but does not alter the guard under test, and the fields the handler touches are individually lock- or atomic-protected (S14). Counterevidence: none of the open issues is evidence against the encoded predicate; the deliberate-design alternative and the threading comment discrepancy are recorded below as limitations.
limitations: The fast path was reached by invoking processHeartbeat, the body of the transport callback, rather than by sending a heartbeat over net_transport, because the fast path exists only there and network access is disabled; the transport's heartbeat classification is a sourced premise (S43) rather than an executed step.
The node has no running main loop, so this comparison does not exercise simultaneous execution of the handler and the main thread; it isolates the guard decision only.
Whether an out-of-window peer can exist in a legal deployment, and the consequence on elections, are outside this check.

review_items.rationale: The checked antecedent is declared before any result is read: the scenario fixes a pure heartbeat shape and a request header version of 0 against a node configured at ProtocolVersionMax, which S42 rejects because it is below the supported window, and the monitor only evaluates when out_of_window_protocol_version is true. The scenario was not selected or filtered by the observed outcome, and no applicability condition depends on guard_applied. limitations: The carrier is one node per path, with no peer, no transport invocation and no main loop; the observation is a handler-level comparison.
The threading comment discrepancy and the deliberate-design alternative for the missing guard remain unresolved boundaries.

resolutions.rationale: The condition records a real conflict on a neighbouring axis: processHeartbeat's comment states it must only be called from the main thread (S40), while the same function is installed as the transport heartbeat callback (S16) and net_transport invokes it from the connection goroutine (S43), with the library's own integration test also calling it from a custom handler (S44). That conflict is about the concurrency contract of the handler, not about which guard it applies. It is answered here as an outer boundary: the obligation under review is the RPC-header compatibility decision, and the completed execution isolates that decision by running the handler with no main loop at all, so the threading question neither validates nor invalidates the observed difference. The guard discrepancy itself is unaffected: the same request shape is rejected with ErrUnsupportedProtocol on the normal path and acted on by the fast path.

condition_dispositions.rationale: Concurrency safety of the fast path is a separate property from the guard it applies. The claim's scope already excludes it, the harness removes concurrent execution so it cannot influence the comparison, and the conflict is retained in this review's limitations rather than deleted or renamed into the claim.

scope_limitations: Whether processHeartbeat may legitimately run off the main thread, and whether its comment is stale or the installation is unsafe, remains an open concurrency question for a different obligation.

resolutions.rationale: This is the harness-level record of the same threading conflict, so it is answered with the same attributed reading instead of a second disposition. The harness legality already declares the adaptation: nodes are built with skipStartup (S46) so the handler is driven without racing a main loop, and the callback seam is justified by the library's own use of r.processHeartbeat(rpc) inside a heartbeat handler (S44). The harness therefore neither depends on nor asserts the concurrency contract that the condition disputes; the driver does not weaken the obligation or the oracle, and the observed difference stands on the guard comparison alone.

condition_dispositions.rationale: The condition targets the threading of the handler, while the harness exercises the guard decision with all background goroutines disabled. It is a boundary of the check rather than a defect in the driver, and it is preserved in the review limitations.

scope_limitations: The check establishes the fast path's guard behaviour only for a node whose main loop is not running; concurrent execution remains untested here.
